episodes.207217: Heavy rain over a several day period caused flash flooding for much of the Tooele Valley. Rainfall totals through the event ranged from 2-4 inches.
episodes.207529: A strong cold front moving across the forecast area on October 4th lead to widespread precipitation. The Nebraska panhandle was in the warm sector ahead of the front, leading to increased moisture and instability. A few thunderstorms developed, including one severe storm in the southern panhandle.
episodes.207718: Amplified troughing was in place over the region, allowing for high based and windy thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.208057: A waterspout was observed over Lago Guajataca in Quebradillas during the afternoon hours of October 4th. The waterspout remained over the lake, and no impacts or damage were reported.

events.narrative: A wind gust of 59 mph was recorded at the Groome mesonet site.

The Rose Park and Sir Phillip Drive areas were hardest hit by flooding, with more than 2 dozen homes flooded when a canal overtopped. Salt Lake City completed a disaster declaration. As of this writing, dollar amount of damages are still being compiled. Rainfall totals ranged from 1-3 inches.

An NWS employee reported flooding of area roads as showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rain in the Tooele Valley. Rainfall totals in the vicinity range from 2-4 inches, with much of that on Saturday, October 4.
The Tooele County EM reported 12 homes with flooding in Tooele and 35 homes total  across eastern Tooele County with some degree of flooding.
The Tooele Co. EM reported significant mud and debris through flood channels leading into  Tooele.
The Tooele Co. EM reported a Union Pacific Railroad track washed over/out from water near Droubay Rd.
Mesonet station AW342 Highlands Ranch observed a 61 mph wind gust with a decaying thunderstorm.
